proposals.before: On one occasion the Emperor summoned the Right Chancellor He Rongzu and the Left Chancellor Ma Shao to turn in all their illicit gains. Siming followed with the documents in his arms. Night had fallen, yet the Emperor ordered them read aloud, and listened from dusk until dawn without tiring. He remarked, "The reader's delivery sounds very much like one of our Ceremonial Institute ushers."
proposals.after: On one occasion the Emperor summoned the Right Chancellor He Rongzu and the Left Chancellor Ma Shao to deliver in full the confiscated illicit gains. Siming followed with the documents in his arms. Night had fallen, yet the Emperor ordered them read aloud, and listened from dusk until dawn without tiring. He remarked, "The reader's delivery sounds very much like one of our Ceremonial Institute ushers."
proposals.reason: 其贓 is the confiscated wealth of Ahmad's clique being delivered in, not illicit gains belonging to He Rongzu and Ma Shao.

proposals.before: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to submit all their bribes in full; Siming carried documents and followed. The day had already grown dark; he ordered them read aloud—from dusk until dawn. The Emperor listened, forgetting fatigue, and said: "The reader's enunciation greatly resembles a Ceremonial Institute usher."
proposals.after: One day he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to submit all the illicit gains in full; Siming carried documents and followed. The day had already grown dark; he ordered them read aloud—from dusk until dawn. The Emperor listened, forgetting fatigue, and said: "The reader's enunciation greatly resembles a Ceremonial Institute usher."
proposals.reason: 盡輸其贓 refers to delivering Ahmad's confiscated goods, not He and Ma submitting their own bribes.

proposals.before: Once Cheng and Li were in the hands of the judicial officials, Siming pressed the Chancellor hard on their behalf, and the two received lighter sentences.
proposals.after: Once Cheng and Li were in the hands of the judicial officials they were due to be judged according to the law; the Chancellor then spoke forcefully on their behalf, and the two received lighter sentences.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 丞相乃力言之 makes the Chancellor, not Siming, the agent who spoke for leniency; the idiomatic English reverses that agency.

proposals.before: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: He was soon promoted to judge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: 樞密院判官 is the office of judge/signatory of the Bureau, not 同知/vice director, which the same biography has already used for Anbo.

proposals.before: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: Soon he was promoted to Judge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: The literal line likewise renders 判官 as Vice Director, colliding with 同知樞密院事 in s0067.

proposals.before: In 1324 he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjian, "Loyal and Simple."
proposals.after: In 1324 he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjian, "Loyal and Simple."
proposals.reason: The Chinese grants 柱國 (Pillar of State) among the Taiding-year honors, which the literal rendering includes but the idiomatic English omits.

proposals.before: Three years later he received the additional honors of meritorious subject who sincerely assisted governance, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.
proposals.after: In 1326, the third year of Taiding, he received the additional honors of meritorious subject who sincerely assisted governance, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: 三年 is the third year of Taiding (AD 1326), not an interval of three years after 1324, which would be misread as 1327.

proposals.before: A former prefect who had risen to assistant administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat quarreled with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and sought to trap him. He shifted Pingjiang's annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand sacks of grain and cloth onto Shaoxing, and the people could not bear the burden.
proposals.after: A former prefect who had risen to assistant administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat quarreled with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and sought to trap him. He shifted Pingjiang's annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand cloth sacks of grain onto Shaoxing, and the people could not bear the burden.
proposals.reason: 布囊 are cloth sacks used for the maritime grain quota, not a combined cargo of grain and cloth.

proposals.before: A former prefect who had become Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat disputed with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and bore a grudge, wishing to entrap him in guilt. He shifted to Shaoxing the annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand sacks of grain and cloth from Pingjiang, requiring Shaoxing to supply the same amount; the people suffered bitterly and could not endure it.
proposals.after: A former prefect who had become Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat disputed with Sheng over substitute grain salaries and bore a grudge, wishing to entrap him in guilt. He shifted to Shaoxing the annual maritime transport quota of thirty thousand cloth sacks of grain from Pingjiang, requiring Shaoxing to supply the same amount; the people suffered bitterly and could not endure it.
proposals.reason: 布囊 means the grain was packed in cloth sacks, not that cloth was part of the levy.

proposals.before: A year later he was recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Blessings with duties at the Divine Imperial Hall, appointed Left Chancellor of Henan, and again transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi circuit.
proposals.after: A year later he was recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Blessings with duties at the Divine Imperial Hall, appointed Left Assistant of the Henan provincial secretariat, and again transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi circuit.
proposals.reason: 河南省左丞 is a provincial left assistant (cheng), not a chancellor (丞相).

proposals.before: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian, "Cultured and Lawful."
proposals.after: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and Left Assistant of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian, "Cultured and Lawful."
proposals.reason: 行中書省左丞 is Left Assistant of the branch secretariat, not Left Chancellor.

proposals.before: The Emperor once sat in the informal hall; when the ministers entered to report affairs and saw Hao, he said with pleasure: "With Chen Zhongming present, what is reported must be good counsel."
proposals.after: The Emperor once sat in the informal hall; when the ministers entered to report affairs, he looked and saw Hao, and said with pleasure: "With Chen Zhongming present, what is reported must be good counsel."
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject of 望見顥 is the seated Emperor, not the entering ministers; the literal English wrongly makes the ministers the ones who saw Hao.

proposals.before: Hao bowed and thanked him, declaring himself unworthy of such trust.
proposals.after: Hao bowed and thanked him, declaring himself unworthy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 謝不敏 only has Hao thanking and calling himself unworthy; 'of such trust' is an added gloss not in the source sentence.

decisions.reason: s0005 has the Secretariat interrogating Ahmad’s remaining clique; 盡輸其贓以入 is He Rongzu and Ma Shao bringing that confiscated wealth in. English “their illicit gains” wrongly makes the two chancellors the owners of the 贓.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 召右丞何榮祖、左丞馬紹，盡輸其贓以入

decisions.reason: 盡輸其贓 continues the Ahmad confiscation, not He and Ma turning in their own bribes. Replacing “their bribes” with “the illicit gains” removes that false possessive.

decisions.after: Once Cheng and Li were in the hands of the judicial officials, they were due to be judged according to the law; the Chancellor then spoke forcefully on their behalf, and the two received lighter sentences.
decisions.reason: 丞相乃力言之 makes the Chancellor the speaker for leniency; the original wrongly has Siming press the Chancellor. The proposal restores agency and 當論法, but needs a comma after “officials.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成、李既屬吏，當論法，丞相乃力言之

decisions.reason: 尋升樞密院判官 is promotion to 判官 of the Bureau of Military Affairs, not vice director (同知). The replacement matches the office name.
The literal line likewise mistranslates 判官 as Vice Director. Judge of the Bureau of Military Affairs is the correct office.
The Taiding honors include 柱國 among 光祿大夫 and 河南等處行省平章政事. The idiomatic English omitted Pillar of State; the replacement restores it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贈光祿大夫、河南等處行省平章政事、柱國

decisions.reason: After 泰定元年, 三年 is the third year of Taiding (1326), not an interval of three years after 1324. The replacement dates the additional honors correctly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三年，復加推誠佐理功臣

decisions.reason: 海運糧布囊三萬 is a maritime grain quota measured in cloth sacks, not grain plus cloth. s0134’s 麻非越土所生 confirms the sacks, not a cloth levy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 移平江歲輸海運糧布囊三萬

decisions.reason: The literal “sacks of grain and cloth” likewise splits 糧布囊 into two cargos. “Cloth sacks of grain” matches 海運糧 packed in 布囊.
河南省左丞 is a provincial left assistant (丞), not 丞相. “Left Chancellor of Henan” conflates the two ranks; Left Assistant of the Henan provincial secretariat is accurate.
贈…河南等處行中書省左丞 is the same 左丞 rank, not Left Chancellor. The replacement restores the posthumous office title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贈資德大夫、河南等處行中書省左丞

decisions.reason: 帝嘗坐便殿…望見顥，喜曰: the seated Emperor is the subject of 望見 and 喜曰. The original English attaches “saw Hao” to the entering ministers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝嘗坐便殿，群臣入奏事，望見顥，喜曰

decisions.reason: 頓首謝不敏 is a polite self-deprecation after the Emperor’s charge to speak without concealment. “Unworthy of such trust” is a contextual gloss of 不敏, not a semantic error; dropping it is stylistic.
